one_liner: Manage and oversee FTA's urban transit grant programs, track congressional appropriations, write program guidance, and brief grantees, elected officials, and congressional staff.
fit_summary: Every grade requires specialized experience with 49 U.S.C. Chapter 53 transit law and formula or discretionary grant programs, which Daniel's resume doesn't show. His FEMA Public Assistance onboarding and county COVID-19 grant applications are grant-adjacent, so GS-11 is a reach and GS-12 and 13 are out.
eligibility: Open to the public (U.S. citizens/nationals) under Direct Hire Authority, so no federal status or veterans' preference is needed.

GS-11 requires one year of GS-09-equivalent experience that includes knowledge of 49 U.S.C. Chapter 53, evaluating program data and legislative requirements, and producing briefs, reports, and oral presentations. Higher grades require applying Chapter 53 to grant programs.
An education-only route exists at GS-11 only (3 years of progressive graduate study toward a Ph.D.), and transcripts are required for it.
No clearance is required, but a background investigation, a one-year probationary period, and a government travel card are conditions of employment.
keywords: evaluating program data and legislative requirements
briefs, technical reports, and oral presentations
strategy: Apply only at GS-11 unless your resume documents at least a year of grant work at a GS-11 equivalent level. Self-rating as an expert without that backing will get the claims disallowed.

Frame your IEM work around any federal grant frameworks you used (Stafford Act, FEMA PA/HMGP, 2 CFR 200, OMB Uniform Guidance), along with grantee and subrecipient support, compliance reviews, and data analysis. Only include what you actually did.

Be honest about Chapter 53 transit law; his resume has none. If he applies, lead with the federal grant program work (FEMA Public Assistance, county COVID-19 grants) and say plainly that transit is new to him.

Preview the questionnaire now. Every narrative answer must open with your title, organization, MM/YYYY–MM/YYYY dates, full- or part-time status, and hours per week exactly as they appear on your resume.

Keep the resume to two pages, and list dates, hours per week, and specialized-experience keywords for each job. The posting runs only Oct 22–Nov 2, 2026, so submit early and confirm all documents uploaded.
resume_bullets: Helped counties update their applications for COVID-19 emergency grants at the start of the pandemic (2020).
Helped sequence onboarding for FEMA Public Assistance employees by organizing spreadsheets and analyzing the data for decision makers (2019–2020).
Tracked state implementation of the Rural Health Transformation Program from November 2025, identifying which states were executing well and which were struggling.
interview_questions: Describe your experience administering formula or discretionary federal grants and ensuring compliance with federal regulations.
How would you explain a new program requirement created by legislation to grantees and congressional staff?
Tell us about a time you analyzed program data to recommend an operational change.
What do you know about FTA's urbanized area formula program and 49 U.S.C. Chapter 53?
watch_outs: The application window is short (closes Nov 2, 2026), and HR will disallow any narrative claim your resume doesn't support.
The Chapter 53 and grants specialized experience requirement is the main barrier to qualifying.
The job is in Washington, DC with telework but no remote option, so expect a commute from Manassas plus some travel.
